newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk policemen charged with casino boss murder.
newsitem.headline: Turk policemen charged with casino boss murder.

text.p: Three Turkish policemen were charged on Thursday with involvement in the murder of a casino owner as part of a security scandal linking the state with criminal gangs, Anatolian news agency said.
"Casino-King" Omer Lutfu Topal was found shot dead in his car in Istanbul last July.

The media has said the three policemen, bodyguards of government MP Sedat Bucak, killed the casino owner in a battle over laundered money from the heroin trade. Topal was alleged to have given money to Kurdish separatist rebels.
The suspects rejected the charges, the agency said. .
The men also went on trial on Tuesday along with seven others on a separate charge of forming an armed gang threatening the security of the state.
The security scandal erupted last November when a car crashed in the western town of Susurluk killing a wanted gangster, a top police officer and a former beauty queen.
Sedat Bucak, who also heads a pro-state Kurdish militia, was in the same car but survived.
The accident spurred a series of media reports that painted a picture of gangsters using state privileges and political connections to kill opponents, trade drugs and traffic in guns.
Interior Minister Mehmet Agar resigned after the media implicated him in the affair. He and Bucak remain government MPs.
